$comment: languages-world-1 (10 November 2026): the WhatsApp allergen guard’s trigger words for KOREAN (ko-KR): 알레르기 / 알러지, 불내증, 과민, 셀리악, 아나필락시스, 글루텐프리 / 무글루텐 / 락토프리, 없는 ("X 없는 메뉴"), 안 들어간 / 들어있지 않 / 포함되지 않 / 미함유, 빼 주세요, 못 먹, 안전, 교차오염, 미량 — stems only, written with and without the space. Bare 빼고 and 제외 are NOT stems ("월요일 빼고" = except Monday); 빼주 / 빼고 주 / 빼고 만들 are. The Unicode normaliser decomposes Hangul into jamo on both sides, so a stem still matches its own syllables. OPTION B, as every other language: absence / safety words only, NOT the bare allergen names (a presence question may reach the AI, which answers only from the tags and gets the caveat). Matched with the Unicode normaliser. caveatWords: a tagged label of the codex allergen set (stored in English, lower case) → the words a reply may use for it (matched on the raw lower-cased reply, so written as the AI writes them). The country has no allergen set of its own yet, so caveatWords are for 'codex' (as MX, SG, HK, MY, TH and AE).
